tag: Episode 42 Side Story · An Ordinary Spring
title: An Ordinary Spring

beats.t: He knew it was a dream because it was too warm. Yeoni's voice calling his name faded, and a night left behind the seal returned. Neo remembered that night. Only this time, it felt as though he could finally send the words he hadn't sent.
A cramped rented room. A phone lay on the desk. Twenty-three-year-old Park Byeongha stared at its screen. One message hovered there, waiting for him to decide whether to send it.
[ Isn't something wrong with your phone? It kept getting notifications earlier. ]
I can tell them tomorrow. That's what I'd thought then too.
This time, his thumb moved first. Send. A tiny paper airplane flew across the screen. Less than a minute later came a reply.
[ Yeoni · OMG yes, it's scary 😭 It keeps sending weird notifications saying it found a vessel. ]
Delete that app now. No, turn off your phone. I'm coming.
He crushed his heels into his shoes and ran. Spring rain had just stopped in the alley. He didn't take an umbrella. This time, even opening one would waste time.
At Yeoni's door, it opened before he could knock. In pajamas, Yeoni held out the phone. The screen blinked on its own.
Look. It turns back on even when I switch it off. I don't even know what app it is.
A black finger protruded from the edge of the screen. He didn't think. He snatched the phone and threw it into the hallway's fire-water bucket. Splash.
My phone!
I'll buy you a new one. In installments.
Installments. You almost managed to look cool.
Something struggled once inside the bucket, then went quiet. He hid his shaking hands in his pockets. Even in a dream, they shook.
Lock your door tonight. See you at the bus stop in the morning.
Why, you're coming with me? You usually board one stop earlier.
Tomorrow, I'll wait.
Morning. Rain. He had arrived first beneath the bus-stop roof, white umbrella fully open. Five whole minutes early.
Seo Hanbi ran up, hugging an envelope. Yeoni followed: yellow bag, wet sneakers. Both were smiling.
Halfie, who's that? His umbrella's huge.
The person who drowned my phone yesterday.
Is that an introduction you should give with a smile?
Park Byeongha. The umbrella is large. It fits three.
The three stood beneath one umbrella. Their shoulders got a little wet. Nobody cared. Banknotes rustled inside the envelope. The words Go to the sea together didn't blur.
We're going to the sea next month. Want to come? There's a contribution.
Oh, let's bring Byeongha! We need someone to carry our bags.
Does the porter get his fee waived?
I'll put it in the ledger. Porter: outstanding.
Yeoni laughed brightly. Seo Hanbi laughed too. In that laughter, he heard his name. Hey, Byeongha. Lightly. At no cost.
So it could have been this easy.
The back seat of the bus. The three sat side by side. Seo Hanbi put the envelope on her knees and began counting notes. Yeoni counted along on their fingers.
This is my share. From here, Halfie's. Exactly half each.
Wow. We're really going to the sea. I don't have a swimsuit.
Just put your feet in. It's still the sea with only your feet in.
He rested his head against the window and watched them. Their counting mingled with the rain. Ten thousand, twenty thousand, thirty thousand. Dull, ordinary numbers. Their ordinariness dazzled him.
Byeongha, what will you do at the sea?
Sit on the sand and guard your bags.
An actual porter.
Porter's the best position. You can see everything.
As he said it, he knew. This was a spring he had never reached. This bus would never arrive at the sea. The dream would end first. Still, he didn't get off. He wanted even one more stop.
Campus. The cherry blossoms were half open. They weren't late for class. Outside the lecture room, Yeoni turned to him.
You look a bit like a cat, you know.
That's a new one.
Not just any cat. A cat in a hat? A white one.
I'll take that as a compliment. Leaving out sleepy and lazy.
Then I'll give you a nickname. Something catlike. Nabi? No. What would be good?
Yeoni rested a finger against their chin and thought. Watching that face, he suppressed a smile. He knew the answer. A name he had been called for a very long time.
Neo. How's that? No idea where I heard it, but it feels right.
The moment the name was spoken, the dream shook. Cherry petals stopped in midair. People's voices went silent. Only Yeoni's remained, coming from outside the dream.
Neo. Hey, Neo. Wake up. I told you, one star.
Ah, right. This was a dream.
The Yeoni in the dream was still smiling. He looked at that face once more. A spring when he wasn't late. An umbrella shared by three. A name that cost nothing.
Thank you. I had a good time.
Cherry petals began falling again. Upward, not down. The dream unraveled into the sky.
Clunk. Wheels rattled. He opened his eyes to Yeoni looking down from the next seat, eyes swollen. His head rested on their shoulder.
He's awake. You're awake! You didn't wake up all day!
“Too loud. My ears hurt.”
That's your first line? One star. Seriously.
They were aboard the chariot of Card Seven. Drawn by two sphinxes, it raced between cards. Moka, Yundal, and Seo Hanbi clung to its luggage compartment.
Awake? The chariot drives itself. We passed Eight through Fifteen overnight.
Before the Strength card, Yeoni covered your eyes with their hand, Mr. Cat. Afraid its light would wear you away again.
Didn't sleep all night. Kept counting your breaths in case they stopped.
I wasn't counting! Just listening!
“How many?”
Twelve hundred and something. I lost count once and started again.
Instead of speaking, Neo rested his forehead against the back of Yeoni's hand. It was a little warmer now than in the dream.
The chariot stopped abruptly. The way was blocked. Beneath black clouds stood a tall tower, lightning coiled around its summit. Number Sixteen, the Tower.
“That place...” Neo pushed himself upright in the seat. “You mustn't go in alone. Whatever happens.”
